column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, idea 1's evidence and a real relation: Carnegie took a town's promise of future taxes for running costs, IPS l.11 refuses anybody else's money and buys the payments first; fix the use column: the 27 of 82 is an October 1916 count and 21 of the 27 paid after warnings, so say a third had failed to make good by then, never that a third broke for good; Indiana had none; her payments are a base for running the residency, never the running money whole (H9-119).

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 store, a magnitude aha: ten years of Carnegie's 10% equal his gift once and Johnson still found it inadequate; fix the figure: 4.3 times sets $500,000 of face against the $115,000 top, so say face dollars or use $399,089 (NUMBERS reserve line), about 3.5 times (as Q100-020's note); Johnson's report itself unread; the sizing is the case's, not Caplet's decision.

Thu 19 Nov: store; Utah's 87% against 65% says running money set before the building helped libraries last, but one state, a nomination form and town size confound it; supports row 1, decides nothing in the IPS.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3d, one clause: Laura splits Carnegie's own rule, doing all for the ten payments and assisting for the building (case l.84-86); a clean structural mapping; never say co-sponsors must carry running costs (Q67-009).
Thu 19 Nov: store; giving in her lifetime is the case's given, not a Caplet choice; Tilden and the Franklin heirs' suit are colour; owned is not committed (SD-3's weakness).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or CONCEIT, a true fact behind the working word pencil: Franklin's codicil writes its condition into the figure (if it succeeds as projected); pairs with row 7, which carries the aha; the codicil's numbers are known compound-interest lore.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c's aha with row 6: the patron saint of compound interest projected a figure that still needed interest to earn it and it fell well short, which is why no figure is stated before the move (NUMBERS 4); fix: one base before any figure (61% on the court's $298,602.04 by Keel's conversion, 67% only from an excerpt), so say well short or about three-fifths; the cause was a lack of borrowers, not a market fall.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 store or with row 9; Boston split the work the other way (founder's money for the building, a co-funder's bonds for running costs); Carnegie's bonds were an endowment, so never call her reserve one; quote Carnegie's 'I'll match' only as his words, never match for co-sponsors (WORDS).

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3a, the card's lead aha: the same man tried promised running money (towns) and owned running money (Boston bonds), and IPS l.11 chooses owned; fix: never experiment or test (two eras, one city); Boston's fund spent only income and lasted partly because a court held its trustees, so never say owned money lasted because owned; Ohio as row 1's fix; H9-119 wording; competes for one outside name in its part.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, one clause at most as row 7's break: the court called Franklin's missed figure unimportant because nobody relied on it, while co-sponsors will plan around Laura's (case l.114); row 21 carries the reliance relation more strongly.

Thu 19 Nov: Seneca's saving clause is idea 3 with row 12; the silent exception and the co-sponsors' discount make row 12 the one to use; keep the two reasons and the ways a promise fails as two lists (card Q109).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d, one clause: every founder's figure carries Seneca's unspoken if I can, if I ought, if things stay so, co-sponsors discount for it (Q139-001), and IPS l.17 names its two exits aloud with a market fall excluded; say no fall in share prices can lower the stated range, never cannot move (NUMBERS 3: an early fund end at zero interest); owned is not committed.
Thu 19 Nov: the large-promise point is row 12's discount said again; Seneca's case is an unworthy receiver, not a changed fortune, so it travels with row 12 or stays in the store.

Thu 19 Nov: store; fix the use: Seneca's two-sided rule asks a giver to give all he is able, and the half kept is held back from the statement, not from the building (CANON D12), so never defend half as Seneca's middle; the half stays Caplet's choice in a nearly one-for-one trade (NUMBERS 8o, about $5,300 per $5,000, checked).

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3b, one clause: Alexander's city in the pocket is the $1 building (Q51-014, 65% saw budgets more than double), so paying toward running costs first makes the building a gift the residency can hold; the upkeep link is Keel's; her payments are a base, not the whole budget (H9-119).

Thu 19 Nov: store; fix: say the plan's order, not the IPS's, since the extra Treasuries are the report's answer to the operating reserve (never inside IPS l.13's step); Cicero's next of kin are family, so the mapping is Keel's and pedigree only.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d: the one who hesitated comes next to the one who refused, so the move on 1 January 2031 (NUMBERS 8r) makes her figure ready at the first meeting; ready means owned, not handed over (paid 2033); English is Keel's.

Thu 19 Nov: store; fix: never say the residency need not ask anyone for running money for ten years, since her payments are a base for running it, not its whole budget (H9-119: never operations owned or the only ask); Maimonides' highest gift is permanent, hers ends in 2042.
Thu 19 Nov: store; pedigree for the case's own flexibility line (l.102-103); the inversion against IPS l.11 is neat but serves no part beyond what the case says; no fraction can be tested.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store or SD-3's evidence: Rome made the city carry the risk that a founder's fortune fell (a ruined donor owed a fifth), and the move takes that risk off the stated range; say it of share prices only; nothing binds Laura legally (case l.114).

Thu 19 Nov: 3d store: reliance turns a promise into a debt (Digest 50.12.1.4), so stating only what she owns keeps what co-sponsors rely on within her holdings; the stronger form of row 10's contrast; Roman law, never Taiwan law; never cannot move (NUMBERS 3).
Thu 19 Nov: store only; pollicitatio names a one-sided promise, so her 2031 statement must stand on what she holds; only a word, as the card says.

Thu 19 Nov: SD-3's evidence clause in 3d: AD 112, every donor's promise for Nicaea's theatre waited on the work which had to be finished first, and Trajan ruled donors pay only once the core stood; maps last money onto Laura's figure first and unconditional; the break (a sinking building) is row 25's limit; 3d's slot is the comfort letter, so this goes with SD-3.
Thu 19 Nov: Trajan's ruling is the reply to row 23's letter and travels in the same sentence; its LACMA and December 2032 links are already Q67-042 and SD-7.
Thu 19 Nov: 3e limit, one clause at most: owned money removes the money reason a building stalls, never the building's own; a caveat, and facility costs are outside the case (l.164).

Thu 19 Nov: SD-3 store: the kula's opening and clinching gifts name first money and last money (case l.112; Kresge as clinching, Q11c-016); the break is apt, co-sponsors give to the building, so her gift opens by example and binds no one; report words stay first and unconditional, never match, anchor or backstop.

Thu 19 Nov: store; a pledge stakes the giver's face is pedigree for case l.114's credibility; fix: never a pledge she can always redeem (NUMBERS 3: an early fund end at zero interest can leave the top short), say owned; Q67's cut figures carry the evidence.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 or 3a store: the ten payments are credit the residency extends to Laura, and IPS l.9 and l.11 move that credit off a writer's income onto the US Treasury; Mauss names what store H1-015 and Q150-021 say in finance terms, so one clause at most beside them.
Thu 19 Nov: store; David's of mine own is pedigree for IPS l.15's money you already own and for the lead gift (H9-129); in Taiwan the founder pays first, never the largest share (Q11e).
Thu 19 Nov: store; Ecclesiastes on vows is textbook pedigree for no figure before the move; one clause or none.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; a campaign that stopped at enough; Laura's top comes from what she owns, not the building's need; call what lies above the top her flexibility (WORDS).

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 store: MacDowell ran on its founder's career and Yaddo on its founders' investments, the two risks IPS l.9 and l.11 refuse in turn; a join of verified store rows (Q9-020, Q9-021), not re-read; both lasted, so it shows the risk run, not a failure.
Thu 19 Nov: 3a, one clause: Keynes's own example of a calculable risk was a government bond's drawing, and Laura's bonds take even the draw out; pairs with row 3, which carries the aha.
Thu 19 Nov: the Gazette fact (Victory Bonds repaid by annual drawings by lot) is row 1's footnote and travels with it.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a and 3b, the card's best aha: Keynes's we simply do not know names the long interest rate and copper, and the plan meets them in opposite ways, buying out of any later rate (from January 2028 the ten are met even if cash waiting earns nothing, NUMBERS 2) and giving the building, about 70% materials in its October rise (Q131), only room (IPS l.15); the break is row 4's: the plan chose the day it meets rates.
Thu 19 Nov: the rate half of row 3 with its break (IPS l.13 completes from the 2028 deposit); the plan facts check against NUMBERS 2 and AHA row 5; use inside row 3's clause.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3e: the building is where the plan admits Keynes's copper and answers with room, not a forecast; its honest limit is NUMBERS 8q (the 1-in-20 joint rise is about her whole flexibility); Q131's metal share makes copper nearly literal.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store: Keynes's three conventions touch only pencil; J.P. Morgan's 7.5% shapes the forecast of the top, never a stated figure, and at 5% the top still states $115,000 (NUMBERS 8v, checked); say above the middle of published forecasts, no median figure.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3f's check: Keynes's weight separates the first plan's 96.8 in 100, resting on a model of share returns (NUMBERS 8s, checked), from none, resting on contracts held to their dates; never as why the plan changed (IPS l.9, CANON A3); weight has no unit.
Thu 19 Nov: Keynes's we cannot measure the increase only tells the report to price what it can (1 in 31, NUMBERS 8s) and name the rest once; a framing note for row 7.

Thu 19 Nov: store; Keynes's heaven or hell against mediocrity is a sharp line against sizing promises by expected value, but the fixed $50,000 is the case's requirement, so it explains no Caplet decision.
Thu 19 Nov: Knight's risk and uncertainty definitions are textbook and already H3-061.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a, one clause with row 16: Knight's single instance (no difference for conduct between measured and unmeasured odds) is the one-path idea of store H4-005 and H5-002 in an uncontested source; Knight's own reservation (however unique the instance) is the break; never as why the plan changed (CANON A3).

Thu 19 Nov: 3a store: the usual road from chance to certainty is grouping many cases, Laura's ten cannot be grouped, and US law's road for a fixed schedule ends at any obligation of the United States (H3-069); an annuity would group but puts an insurer in between.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3, one clause: Knight's two incomes map onto IPS l.9: her career is residual income, her promises are paid only from contractual income (Treasuries), and the half kept is her residual; the break is apt (her guarantor issues the currency; the half kept is room, not a reward).
Thu 19 Nov: Knight's pledging his own earning power is the route IPS l.9 closes and is the second half of row 13's clause; say her income can fall in the same downturn, never together.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3f store: Bernoulli's moral certainty (999/1000, the line left to magistrates) is the origin of the scale the case's high sits on, and the polled judges and the SEC near 90% (Q120) show nobody fixed it; IPS l.11 is the only definition of high (CANON A4); 999/1000 read only in Hubert's quotation.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a with row 11: certainty from probability takes repetition (Bernoulli's 25,550 draws) and each payment falls once; Bernoulli's draws learn a ratio, so never say Laura would need thousands of payments.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Descartes's moral and absolute certainty is read only in Hubert's quotation, so read Cottingham at source before use; row 32 already says the plan claims a conditional.

Thu 19 Nov: Peters's ensemble against one path is the store's coin (H4-060) and H4-005; economists contest his wider claim (row 20), so Knight's sentence carries it; his multiverse line at most as colour.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store: the move is the day the average across futures becomes her own path; restates NUMBERS 4's why nothing is stated before the move (10.6% at 12 months, checked, worded as the move buying less than a top stated early); leans on Peters, so say it without him.
Thu 19 Nov: store guard only: economists reject Peters's ergodic programme (Doctor, Wakker and Wang 2020, read only in the university's summary); a caveat, so F 2.
Thu 19 Nov: Kelly's broke with probability one is the gambler's-ruin point of H4-060; Q123 rows 4 and 6 hold the rest of Kelly.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3b: Savage's two proverbs map onto the dated steps, look before you leap for the ten payments in January 2027 and cross that bridge for the building's figure left to 2031 with half unpromised (IPS l.13, l.15; GOLDMINE 27); the break is honest (his small world is simplified thinking, hers is bought).

Thu 19 Nov: CONCEIT or 3.0: Savage said he could not give criteria for a small world, and the plan's line is ink's own, a promise is in when a Treasury she owns will pay it on its date (IPS l.15); a dissimilar parallel as a true fact behind the word ink, never a new turn; never say the plan answers Savage in general, the team still chose the line.
Thu 19 Nov: Savage's deferred decision is row 22's cross that bridge; card Q154 holds staged commitment.
Thu 19 Nov: Gigerenzer's picnic (ill-defined, not intractable) is a reason clause for row 5's room, not a forecast, and facility estimates are outside the case anyway (l.164).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e frame or store: the IPS's range as a door on a hinge (the top swings with markets, the bottom stays constant, IPS l.15) is a real and startling mapping; fix: it is a second image, and CONCEIT V2.2 takes parallels only as true facts behind single working words, one turn per part, so never a hinge turn beside ink; it holds only before the move.
Thu 19 Nov: 3e or Table 2's note: every test takes the Treasury's payment as given, so no test can test it; where the one doubt is said, a caveat placement, so F 2; IPS l.11 already says it once.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; a philosopher's reason for Book 19's rule against attaching the doubt to every figure; an internal wording rule, serves no part.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e with row 32: Cromwell's rule allows certainty only by implication, so the plan's certain is a deduction from named premises; certain takes the Treasuries or the stated range as subject, never a dollar figure (WORDS).

Thu 19 Nov: 3c or 3d store: a probability is someone's belief while a holding can be shown on a statement (Q22-020), so after the move her range is the showable kind; fix: read de Finetti's 1974 preface at source; the comfort letter holds 3d's slot, so this is its reason clause at most.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e: the test of where ownership converts chance (VT owned but pencil, Q157; building costs fail); fix: the late-2032 fund pays no fixed sum (TNA l.13, l.15), so the ends pass because the margin and the rounding down let its payout be counted, never a fixed dollar sum for an iBond fund; it is ink's definition restated, so one clause at most.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3e, the answer to certain as a trick of words: a forecast's many light premises swapped for a few heavy named ones; fix the list (NUMBERS 8u, 3): the cost premise is the room under each figure (about 2% for the top, about 3% for the bottom), never inside the 0.5% margin; add an early fund end with cash at zero and a broker failure as delay; the ten survive a 2028 deposit about three-quarters smaller; keep it apart from IPS l.17's two reasons.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or Table 2's note: Keynes's own grades place each part (payments beyond roulette, the top before the move with the weather, the building with copper); a one-line map, the mapping Keel's; never cannot move for the stated range (NUMBERS 3).
